text:
Tao L: Noticed multiple regressions in our JS SDK after we tightened the package exports. Next.js SSR sample and a few internal lambda examples started throwing at runtime: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" and some bundlers complain there is no default export.

Nina S: Which consumers are failing? modern bundlers should pick import field, older require-based apps will choke. Do we have a repro?

Tao L: Repro is in samples/next-ssr and samples/lambda-proxy. Steps: yarn && yarn workspace samples-next dev -> server-side render fails when requiring the SDK during SSR. Error traces point at node trying to require the package but resolver picked the ESM path.

Ollie M: Looks like removal of the fallback `./index.cjs` + no `require` conditional triggered this. Also saw TypeScript path resolution break for projects that use `paths` mapping to node_modules entry.

QA Runner: CI alert: several smoke tests in `samples/*` failing since the publish 2.1.2. Failing jobs: next-ssr-smoke, lambda-integration. Logs: ```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
```

Tao L: Here is the exports field from the published package (copied from installed node_modules): ```json
{ ".": {"import": "./esm/index.mjs", "types": "./types/index.d.ts"}, "./*": "./*" }
```
No `require` branch, no cjs entry.

Nina S: Two orthogonal problems: runtime resolution for CJS consumers and TS typing shape for default import. For typings, some projects expect `export = SDK` or a `default` export in d.ts which we removed.

Ollie M: Proposed fixes: 
- Add conditional exports: "require": "./cjs/index.cjs" under `.` so require() uses CJS build. 
- Keep `import` pointing to ESM. 
- Add `typesVersions` or update `index.d.ts` to have `export =` compatibility or `declare const defaultExport: ...; export default defaultExport;`

Tao L: Also we need to avoid regressing edge-only environments (Cloudflare/Workers) that cannot execute CJS bundles. Conditional exports handle that elegantly.

Nina S: Can we instead ship a tiny compat wrapper: `dist/index.mjs` that `export { default } from './index.cjs'` for interop? That sometimes confuses bundlers though. I'd rather add explicit `require` conditional.

Dev Bot: Automated analysis flagged 18 dependent repos that import SDK using `const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk-js')` or `import sdk from '@redwood/sdk-js'`. Top affected: internal-analytics, web-playground, legacy-cli.

QA Runner: Suggest we add two CI jobs in the SDK repo: `compat-cjs` which runs node-based require tests and `edge-esm` which runs wrangler/esbuild smoke for worker runtime. Matrix on node versions (12/14/16) helps catch edge cases.

Ollie M: I'll open a patch PR that restores `require` conditional and adds a small CJS build, plus a d.ts file with `export =` compatibility. Will include a release note.

Tao L: Please also add a small test in samples/next-ssr that runs `node -r ts-node/register samples/next-ssr/test-require.js` to make sure require path works.

Nina S: Confirmed plan: patch -> canary publish `canary/exports-compat` -> run samples CI and notify teams found by Dev Bot. After a week we can remove compat in a major release if desired, but must communicate widely.

Dev Bot: CI run queued for PR #238 (canary publish), tracking id: cb-exports-compat-238.

Ollie M: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/238 (adds conditional require + d.ts compatibility + CI matrix). Will ping for reviews.

QA Runner: Good. Also add a short migration note in docs/sdk/migrating-exports.md with recommended import patterns and a snippet: ```ts
// preferred for ESM-aware consumers
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js';

// for legacy require consumers
const SDK = require('@redwood/sdk-js');
```

Tao L: Thanks all. Let's prioritize the patch so downstream samples and customers don't break unexpectedly. :shipit:
